chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abdul Hameed ibn Awwaz al-Taiy, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who marries the woman, but he does not have with him what he can give her, so he enters into her (consummates the marriage). He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem; it is merely a debt for her upon him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man marries and consummates the marriage before paying the dowry?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that consummating marriage prior to the actual payment of the dowry (*mahr*) is legally permissible, establishing the unpaid amount as a binding debt (*dayn*) rather than a condition for validity. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding marital contracts, prioritizing the wife's financial right as a secured debt over immediate liquidity. It reflects the practical reality of early Muslim communities where immediate payment was often not feasible, ensuring the wife's rights remained protected regardless of the timing of payment.
